title: Verifiable Quantum Advantage and Computation via Quantum Circuit Obfuscation
authors: Alexandru Gheorghiu, Aparna Gupte, Vojtěch Havlíček, Yunchao Liu
abstract: We construct protocols for classically verifiable quantum advantage and classical verification of $\mathsf{BQP}$ computations using \emph{quantum indistinguishability obfuscation} (qiO). Specifically, given qiO and assuming a slightly stronger version of $\mathsf{BQP}\neq\mathsf{BPP}$, we construct a two-message quantum-advantage protocol that is efficiently and publicly verifiable. Our result can be viewed as a rigorous cryptographic foundation for the heuristic quantum advantage proposals based on \emph{peaked random circuit sampling} of Aaronson and Zhang (arXiv:2404.14493).   We also construct two simple protocols for classically verifying arbitrary $\mathsf{BQP}$ computations. The first protocol is privately verifiable and assumes only the existence of qiO. This gives a rare example of a nontrivial cryptographic application of (quantum) iO that does not make additional computational hardness assumptions. The second protocol additionally assumes post-quantum one-way functions and is \emph{publicly verifiable}. To our knowledge, this is the first publicly verifiable protocol for classical verification of $\mathsf{BQP}$ computations under computational assumptions in the standard model.   We show that all our results hold when qiO is assumed only for ancilla-free unitary circuits. As evidence supporting this assumption, we prove a worst-to-average-case reduction for obfuscating such circuits. This reduction extends the local-mixing framework of Canetti, Chamon, Mucciolo and Ruckenstein (TCC 2024) under quantum analogues of their assumptions.
summary: This work establishes rigorous cryptographic protocols for proving and verifying quantum computational advantage. By leveraging Quantum Indistinguishability Obfuscation (qiO), the authors construct schemes that allow classical parties to verify the results of BQP computations, achieving both private and publicly verifiable standards. This provides a strong theoretical foundation for the concept of quantum advantage.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of creating protocols that allow classical verification of quantum computational advantages and the results of BQP computations.
main_result: They construct a publicly verifiable two-message quantum-advantage protocol and develop protocols for both private and public classical verification of arbitrary BQP computations.
method: The core method relies on utilizing Quantum Indistinguishability Obfuscation (qiO) to build cryptographic foundations for quantum advantage proofs and verification schemes.
model_or_system: The model involves abstract quantum circuits and the complexity class BQP (Bounded-error Quantum Polynomial time). The security is analyzed using quantum indistinguishability and the diamond distance.
key_observables: Quantum indistinguishability ($	ext{qiO}$), quantum advantage proof success probability, and the ability to distinguish between quantum and classical computation.

paper_structure: The paper builds from the general problem of verifiable quantum advantage, first constructing a two-message protocol, then detailing private verification using only $	ext{qiO}$, and finally achieving the first publicly verifiable protocol by adding post-quantum assumptions.
why_interesting: While highly theoretical, the rigorous cryptographic framework developed for verifying quantum computation provides deep insights into the computational separation between classical and quantum resources, which underpins much of modern quantum information theory.
